unit_name: Army Group G (Heeresgruppe G; Armeegruppe G until late 1944)

Renamed the 16th Volksgrenadier Division (GER-VG-016D) on 9 October 1944 in the Vosges and almost completely re-formed (Lexikon; lineage UL024). Formal national command of the Dutch Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten (Netherlands Forces of the Interior; also Nederlandse Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten, NBS), entered under Scott's irregular-forces rule (HANDOFF standing rule 21) after his approval of 14 November 2026 on branch small-fixes-1113. NIMH, De oprichting van de Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten (R1163, opened 14 November 2026): on 31 August 1944 SHAEF, at Queen Wilhelmina's wish and on Prince Bernhard's urging, authorised the formation of the BS; Prince Bernhard became its commander-in-chief, under Eisenhower; on 5 September 1944 (Dolle Dinsdag) the BS was established by Royal Decree, uniting the LKP, RVV and OD. The same page records that the BS was a temporary organisation, to be dissolved three months after the German capitulation, and that it was dissolved on 8 August 1945. A second family, the Dutch Wikipedia article Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten (R1164, opened 14 November 2026), also dates the official founding to 5 September 1944 and names Prince Bernhard as commander; it gives the dissolution only as August 1945. The veterans' site binnenlandsestrijdkrachten.nl (opened 14 November 2026, not given its own reference id) cites Koninklijk Besluit Staatsblad E62 of 5 September 1944 and Bernhard's appointment as Bevelhebber der Nederlandse Strijdkrachten on 3 September, and places his headquarters first in London, later in Brussels, and in November 1944 at Breda (staff in a tax office; himself at landgoed Anneville). Those headquarters statements are not used as location claims: they describe the Bevelhebber's staff, are dated only as November for Breda, and London is not a place already in the dataset. NIMH's statement that Bernhard was under Eisenhower is not entered as a command relation to SHAEF (ALL-SHAEF-000H): a second independent family opened for this pass (Dutch Wikipedia; the veterans' site) does not name SHAEF or Eisenhower as the BS's superior, and the 16 May 1944 civil-affairs agreement on liberated territory is not by itself an assignment of this formation. parent_unit_id is left blank. The Stoottroepen and Bewakingstroepen are recorded as organic components from the 22 September 1944 split south of the great rivers (de Jong, deel 10a, pp. 561-563, R894; NIMH R1163 also names the Stoottroepen as the armed branch of the BS). Lodders and Kraandijk, Militaire Spectator 1994 (R1162): Limburg, by its relationship with the Americans, took increasing distance from Commando Zuid; the three Limburg battalions came under the Koninklijke landmacht section of Prince Bernhard's staff on 2 January 1945 and transferred into the KL in January; Brabant companies were employed by the British from 11 October 1944 and transferred into the KL in May, at which point Commando Zuid was abolished. Those transfers are noted and are not given invented end-days. No new numbered Allied parent is entered for the regional commands. Review (branch small-fixes-1113, 14 November 2026, approved by Scott): old value none, new value this unit. record_status is placeholder (old value would have been active): the unit has no claim file, because no opened source names a place for the 5 September 1944 Royal Decree, and a location claim is not invented. UK-DIST-NETH is the same pattern (a sourced higher command without a location row). The formed date and the command relations stand.

Formal territorial command of the Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten in Noord-Holland north of the IJ (gewest 11), entered under Scott's irregular-forces rule (HANDOFF standing rule 21) after his approval of 12 November 2026. De Jong, deel 10b, p. 706: around Dolle Dinsdag (5 September 1944) the lieutenant-colonel of infantry (KNIL, retired) J. G. M. Wastenecker, then gewestelijk commandant of the OD, unified the armed resistance in the district; he later appears as commandant of the BS in Noord-Holland Noord (p. 1315). Colonel Koot's orders came through well in this gewest (de Jong citing van Ojen). It published the only BS-gewest narrative in book form (De mannen van overste Wastenecker, 1947). Independent (no parent in the table; the overall BS command under Prince Bernhard and Colonel Koot is not a unit). formed_date 5 September 1944 is "omstreeks Dolle Dinsdag", when de Jong first describes Wastenecker as the district commander (then still of the OD); by April 1945 the same command is the BS gewest. The gewestelijke Stormtroepen of about 200 men (mostly former KP, p. 706) are not entered as a separate unit. Added in the de Jong 10a-1 follow-up 2 (dejong-10a1, 12 November 2026).

Formal guard and rear-area units of the Dutch Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten, entered under Scott's irregular-forces rule (HANDOFF standing rule 21) after his approval of 12 November 2026. De Jong, Het Koninkrijk, deel 10a, pp. 561-563: on 22 September 1944 van Houten split the BS south of the great rivers into Stoottroepen (to fight with the Allies) and Bewakingstroepen (guard duties behind the front and of the camps) and gave command of the Bewakingstroepen to W. J. van Dijk. Independent (no parent), parallel to NL-INF-STOOT. Numbered battalions are not split out: the London return of early May 1945 names two battalions, but de Jong says that count covered only companies already grouped in battalions and is not a complete list of names. De Blauwe Jagers (about 300 former Pan members placed under van Dijk on 25 September, p. 563) are recorded in the private notes and are not a separate unit. Added in the de Jong 10a-1 follow-up 2 (dejong-10a1, 12 November 2026). Review (Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten unit, branch small-fixes-1113, 14 November 2026, approved by Scott): units.csv parent_unit_id old value: blank; new value: blank (unchanged). The Bewakingstroepen are the guard arm of the BS from the same 22 September 1944 split (de Jong, pp. 561-563; C9389), recorded as CR1312 (administrative_control to NL-BS-000H). units.csv parent is left blank for the same reason as NL-INF-STOOT (administrative_control in the relations table, not an organic units.csv parent).

In March 1945 two of its companies went into the Rhineland with the British Second Army; one of those two later advanced with the British towards Bremen (no arrival date is given). Formal combat units of the Dutch Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten, entered under Scott's irregular-forces rule (HANDOFF standing rule 21, 12 November 2026): organised with a command chain and placed at the disposal of Allied commanders. De Jong, Het Koninkrijk, deel 10a, p. 556: Prince Bernhard, on 17 or 18 September 1944, said he intended to group former illegal workers into combat units (stoottroepen) and place them at the disposal of the Allied commanders, and appointed B. J. C. (Bep) van Kooten commander of the Stoottroepen-Limburg; van Kooten was back in Maastricht recruiting on 19 September. p. 561-563: on 22 September van Houten (not then knowing of van Kooten's Limburg appointment) appointed Borghouts commander of the Stoottroepen der Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten south of the great rivers, and gave command of the Bewakingstroepen to van Dijk; the BS were split into Stoottroepen (to fight with the Allies) and Bewakingstroepen (guard duties). formed_date 1944-09-18 is the first of the two days de Jong gives for the prince's instruction and the Limburg appointment (p. 556); the overall command south of the rivers is dated 22 September (p. 561-563). Independent (no parent). Subordinate battalions and the later regular-army regiment are not entered in this first chunk. Added in the de Jong 10a-1 follow-up (dejong-10a1, 12 November 2026). Review (Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten unit, branch small-fixes-1113, 14 November 2026, approved by Scott): units.csv parent_unit_id old value: blank; new value: blank (unchanged). The Stoottroepen are the combat arm of the BS from the 22 September 1944 split (de Jong, deel 10a, pp. 561-563, R894; NIMH, R1163), recorded as CR1311 (administrative_control to NL-BS-000H), not as an organic units.csv parent. organic relations are excluded from build/command_relations.csv and from who_controls; administrative_control is the schema class that records an administrative superior and appears in who_controls. units.csv parent is left blank because C9384 (18 September, still stoottroepen of the OD, parent XXX Corps) predates the split, and a units.csv organic parent would have to appear on every claim that already lists a relation.

Regional command of the Stoottroepen in Noord-Brabant. First documented action: on 10 October 1944 a first company (just over 120 men) under Sjef de Groot went to the Land van Maas en Waal (de Jong, deel 10a, p. 768). De Jong later names de Groot commandant of the Brabantse Stoottroepen; he was dismissed and sent to London some time after the beginning of January 1945, after which the Brabant battalions were likewise converted to light infantry (p. 760). G. H. Bensen is named as acting commander in Noord-Brabant around 1 January (p. 760) but no appointment date is given. Organic parent NL-INF-STOOT. formed_date is the first documented company, not a separately dated charter of the regional command. Added in the de Jong 10a-1 follow-up 2 (dejong-10a1, 12 November 2026).

Regional command of the Stoottroepen der Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten in (South) Limburg, under B. J. C. (Bep) van Kooten, appointed by Prince Bernhard on 17 or 18 September 1944 (de Jong, deel 10a, p. 556); van Kooten was back in Maastricht recruiting on 19 September. Organic parent NL-INF-STOOT. Numbered Limburg battalions are not entered: de Jong refers to "de Zuidlimburgse bataljons" in the plural (p. 769) without giving numbers. Beginning of January 1945 the Limburg battalions were converted to light infantry battalions and the old ranks were reintroduced (p. 760); the new official names are not given, so the unit id is kept (redesignation keeps the id). Added in the de Jong 10a-1 follow-up 2 (dejong-10a1, 12 November 2026). Review (Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten unit, branch small-fixes-1113, 14 November 2026, approved by Scott): Lodders and Kraandijk, Militaire Spectator 1994 (R1162, p. 406) record that on 2 January 1945 the three Limburg battalions came under the control of the Koninklijke landmacht section of Prince Bernhard's staff, and that the Limburgse Stoottroepen transferred into the Koninklijke landmacht in January 1945. No new parent unit is entered for that staff section, and no end day is invented for the organic link through NL-INF-STOOT.

unit_name: Task Force A (1st Tank Destroyer Brigade)
unit_note: Provisional task force of the Third Army formed for the Brittany north shore railway under Brigadier General Herbert L. Earnest, headquarters the 1st Tank Destroyer Brigade, with the 6th Tank Destroyer Group, 15th Cavalry Group and 159th Engineer Battalion, about 3,500 men (Blumenson, Breakout and Pursuit, ch. 21). Provisional mechanised task force of VI Corps under Brigadier General Frederick B. Butler, the deputy corps commander; official designation Provisional Armored Group, VI Corps (Clarke and Smith, ch. 5, n. 6). Dissolved as a separate entity by the 36th Division on 23 August 1944 but used again as a task force until the end of the Montélimar battle; Butler returned to VI Corps afterwards (ch. 10). Brigades Batch 2.
